content.comment_body: I have a smoke sensor with external LED activation, providing a 5V output and a maximum 5mA load. I understand that [product_name] digital inputs require at least 8.5V to register ON, so 5V isn't sufficient to enable the port. What is the recommended way to use a 5V source and activate the [product_name] digital input? Should I use an NPN transistor or a micro relay, considering the load limit? Thank you for your assistance.
Hello, I would recommend considering an optocoupler rather than a relay.
You could use an analog threshold function. Simply connect it to the analog input and process the output using the analog function as needed. Sent from App.
@ [user_name], this works only if a free 0-10V analog input is available.

That's correct—I had considered the 0-10V input option, but all my analog inputs are currently used for pressure sensors. I just purchased an opto-relay 24V board, which I believe will work and plan to test once it arrives. It only cost 5.5 euro for a 4-channel version.

There are also amplifier boards available for around 3 USD on AliExpress. These can boost the voltage to reach logic high for digital inputs on [product_name]. Just another idea to consider. Sent from App.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing how to connect a 5V output from a third-party smoke sensor to the digital input of [product_name], which requires a higher minimum input voltage. The main issue is that the sensor output is not sufficient for the digital input specifications, prompting users to explore external hardware solutions such as optocouplers, relays, and amplifier boards. This highlights a lack of clear documentation or guidance on connecting lower-voltage sources, which affects user decision-making and workflow.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to easily connect third-party sensors with 5V outputs to [product_name] digital inputs, without needing complex solutions. Clear instructions or recommended options for resolving this signal compatibility issue are desired.
